Package de.nexus.antixray.api.event

Class ThrottleLevelChangeEvent

java.lang.Object
org.bukkit.event.Event
de.nexus.antixray.api.event.ThrottleLevelChangeEvent
public class ThrottleLevelChangeEvent extends org.bukkit.event.Event
Called when the self-throttling of NexusAntiXRay (performance.auto-throttle in its config) changes its level.

Level 0 means no throttling. A higher level means that NexusAntiXRay checks less often: hidden blocks, tiles, entities and players are revealed and hidden again a little later. What is hidden, the fake ore veins and the light masking stay the same in every level, and nothing is revealed that a check would not reveal. Today the highest level is 1; later versions may have more levels, so compare with > 0 rather than == 1.

The event reports changes only. None is called while the throttling is switched off, during its start-up period after the server or the plugin starts (60 seconds), when max-level is 0, when NexusAntiXRay is disabled, and for single players. The development switch -Dnexusantixray.throttle.force calls one event with cause ThrottleLevelChangeEvent.Cause.CONFIG when the measurement starts. The event is a notification and cannot be cancelled: the level is a performance measure and is already in effect when the event is called.

Thread

The event is synchronous. On Spigot and Paper it is called on the server thread, in the tick in which the level changed. On Folia it is called on the global region thread. There the level belongs to each player (the tick time of the region the player is in), and the event reports the highest level of all players: getTickMillis() is the value of the player with the highest level, and the event can come up to a second (20 ticks of the global region) after the change of that player. When the only throttled player leaves the server, nobody is throttled any more and the reported level drops at once, with cause ThrottleLevelChangeEvent.Cause.LOAD and the tick time of another player (or NaN when no player is left). A player who logs in again keeps the level they had. It is never called from a network or ray tracing thread.
Since:
1.0.0

      public ThrottleLevelChangeEvent(int oldLevel, int newLevel, ThrottleLevelChangeEvent.Cause cause, double tickMillis, ThrottleLevelChangeEvent.TickSource tickSource)
      Creates the event. NexusAntiXRay calls this constructor; plugins only listen.
      Parameters:
      oldLevel - the level before the change, 0 or more
      newLevel - the level after the change, 0 or more
      cause - why the level changed
      tickMillis - the tick time in milliseconds, normalized to 20 ticks per second, or Double.NaN
      tickSource - where the tick time comes from; null or a NaN tick time give ThrottleLevelChangeEvent.TickSource.UNKNOWN
      Since:
      1.0.0
